we have measured the clustering of gas-rich galaxies, the most weakly clustering population of galaxies known, in a large sample of galaxies selected in a blind fashion.

we have used the Arecibo Legacy fast ALFA survey catalog (alpha.40) of 10,150 H-I-selected galaxies to analyze the clustering characteristics of gas-rich galaxies, and found that they represent the most weaklly clustered galaxy population in the local Universe.

the 40% ALFA survey catalog (α.40) of ~10,150 H I-selected galaxies provides a detailed understanding of the correlation function of gas-rich galaxies, which can be used to constrain models of the distribution and evolution of neutral hydrogen in galaxies and the role of gas-rich galaxies in environmentally dependent galaxy formation.
